chunks: And in the narration of Zurārah from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
"Whoever does that out of forgetfulness, inattentiveness, or ignorance, there is nothing upon him."

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, the Imam transmitting the ruling
key_terms.جَاهِلًا: ignorantly; doing the act without knowledge of the ruling
key_terms.رِوَايَةِ: narration; a reported transmission of the hadith
key_terms.زُرَارَةَ: Zurārah, the narrator transmitting from the Imam
key_terms.سَاهِيًا: inattentively; doing the act absentmindedly or heedlessly
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: anything; here meaning liability or penalty
key_terms.نَاسِيًا: forgetfully; doing the act due to forgetfulness

ai.seo_question: Is there any penalty for a muhrim who does a prohibited act out of forgetfulness or ignorance?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle of exemption from liability when a prohibited act is done unintentionally, through forgetfulness, heedlessness, or ignorance. In the context of the muhrim, it indicates that no penalty is due in such cases.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2690 - In the narration of Zurara from Abu Ja'far (as):
"Whoever does that (trims nails) out of forgetfulness, inattentiveness, or ignorance, there is nothing upon them (no penalty)."
